subject.title: fix(agents): follow through on promised asynchronous work

question: Should OpenClaw accept best-effort prompt guidance for promised asynchronous work, or require an enforceable completion-path invariant at the agent runtime boundary?
rationale: Semantic commitment detection, explicit completion-path state, and response rewriting have different false-positive and compatibility tradeoffs that cannot be selected safely without agent-runtime owner intent.

options.title: Enforce the invariant
options.body: Move the guarantee into terminal outcome or delivery state, keep capability-aware prompt reinforcement, and add focused live proof.

options.title: Accept prompt hardening
options.body: Land this explicitly as best-effort prompt hardening while leaving the broader runtime guarantee to the canonical issue.

options.title: Pause this branch
options.body: Keep the canonical issue open until maintainers select a runtime design, then replace or revise this PR accordingly.

recommendation.title: Enforce the invariant
recommendation.body: Move the guarantee into terminal outcome or delivery state, keep capability-aware prompt reinforcement, and add focused live proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The current planning-only classification and follow-up-delivery behavior appear to originate from this contributor’s merged runtime work.
